messages.author: eb6e32da792b07d0
messages.subject: overfitting in the prediction
parts:
Hi all,

I fit a spatiotemporal Poisson model to counts from 45 villages over 132 months. I am interested in making predictions for the month of 121-132. I used the suggestion from the FAQs (http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-How-can-I-do-predictions-using-INLA-) and included NAs in the month of 121-132. 

When I plot model$summary.fitted.values$mean, the patterns look reasonable for the month of 1-120 but for the predictions seems overfitted (observed vs fitted figures is attached). Am I missing something? I would greatly appreciate any advice on how best to address this.

I have included my code below. 

fCov1 <- den ~ denLag2 + 
  f(ID.area, model="bym", graph=yk.adj) + 
  f(ID.month, model="rw2") + 
  f(ID.month1, model="iid") + 
  f(ID.area.month, model="iid") # Type I interaction

model <- inla(fCov1, family="poisson", data=data, 
                    control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, link=link),
                    control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE))

Best regards
--
Aditya

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] overfitting in the prediction
parts:
Dear Håvard Rue 

I also have the same problem with this. I create a model for forecasting relative risk periods 221-212. The model is pretty good for 1-120. But for the forecasting value, the relative risk is very unreasonable. The value value is very high almost 100. The value should be under 5. 
When I remove the rw2 the model is pretty bad, the smoothing model faild.  


Model12<-Case ~ f(IS0, model = "bym", graph = W)+ f(IT3, model = "rw2")+ f(IT1, model = "iid")+  f(DT, model = "iid") 
ModelRun12 <- inla(Model12,family="poisson",data=DATA18,E=Expected, control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE,link=1)
,control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE))

What should I do to keep the model smooth with rw2 but there is no overfitting problem? 

Thank you very much for your attention. 
Mindra

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] overfitting in the prediction
parts:
Dear Miranda,

I am Haavard's postdoc.

The RW2 model includes a linear trend (in the null-space), which may not be what you want for forecasting. I suggest you try ar1. The ar1 regress to the mean when forecasting far ahead.

I also suggest using more conservative priors. PC priors.

Regards,
Haakon
